In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surah Luqman

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim.﴾ ﴿These are the verses of the Wise Book, a guidance and a mercy for the good-doers.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify His saying, ﴿a guidance and a mercy for the good-doers﴾, at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. That is the Book, in which there is no doubt, a guidance for the God-fearing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 1-2].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly, as if he did not hear them, as if there were deafness in his ears. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.﴾

In this noble verse, exalted and highly exalted is He, mentioned that when the verses of Allah are recited to the disbeliever, and they are this great Qur'an, ﴿he turns away arrogantly﴾, meaning, proud of refusing to accept them, ﴿as if he did not hear them﴾. ﴿As if there were deafness in his ears﴾, meaning, deafness and a heaviness preventing him from hearing them. Then He commanded His Prophet ﷺ to give him tidings of a painful punishment.

Exalted and highly exalted is He has clarified this meaning in many verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾ ﴿who hears the verses of Allah recited to him, then persists arrogantly as if he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment﴾ ﴿And when he learns anything of Our verses, he takes them in ridicule. Those will have a humiliating punishment﴾ ﴿Behind them is Hell, and no avail will they have from what they earned, nor from what they took as protectors other than Allah. And for them is a great punishment﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 7–10]. Here He said, ﴿as if there were deafness in his ears﴾, by way of comparison. In another place He stated explicitly that He actually placed deafness in their ears, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness﴾ [al-Kahf: 57]. The apparent meaning is that the deafness mentioned here is by way of comparison to physical deafness, because the spiritual deafness resembles physical deafness, and the deafness placed upon their ears in actuality is only the spiritual deafness preventing them from hearing the truth, not hearing anything else. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 10:

(p-180) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He created the heavens without pillars that you can see﴾.

We have already explained this with Qur'anic verses at the beginning of Surah "al-Ra'd" (Thunder), in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is Allah who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see﴾ [al-Ra'd: 2].

Allah's statement: ﴿This is the creation of Allah; so show Me what those besides Him have created.﴾

We have already presented the verses clarifying this in Surat ar-Ra'd (al-Ra'd), in the discussion of His statement: ﴿Or have they set up for Allah partners who created like His creation, so that the creation seemed alike to them?﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 16], and at the beginning of Surat al-Furqan.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 13:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] when Luqman said to his son while he was advising him, "O my son, do not associate anything with Allah. Indeed, association [with Him] is great injustice."﴾ This noble verse indicates that shirk (association of partners with Allah) is great injustice (zulm 'azim).

Allah, exalted is He, has explained this in other verses, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not invoke other than Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you. For if you did, then indeed you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ [Yunus: 106], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 254]. It has been established in the Sahih, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he "explained the injustice (zulm) in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who believed and did not mix their belief with injustice (zulm)﴾ [al-An'am: 82], as being shirk," and Allah clarified this with His saying here: ﴿Indeed, association [with Him] is great injustice﴾. We have already clarified this earlier.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 15:

The author said in *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book):

(p-365) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Luqman (the thirty-first chapter of the Qur'an)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And accompany them in this world with kindness﴾.

This noble verse indicates the command to show kindness to disbelieving parents. Another verse has come which appears to imply the opposite, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Mujadila: 22].

Then He explicitly included fathers in this prohibition by His saying: ﴿even if they were their fathers﴾ [al-Mujadila: 22]. What appears to me, and Allah knows best, is that there is no contradiction between the two verses.

The way to reconcile them is that accompanying with kindness is more general than mutual affection, because a person can do good to someone he loves and to someone he does not love. The prohibition of the more specific does not necessitate the prohibition of the more general. So it is as if Allah warned against affection, which implies inner love and allegiance, toward all disbelievers, a category that includes fathers and others, and commanded a person to do for his parents only what is good. Doing good does not necessitate affection, because affection is an action of the hearts, not an action of the limbs.

Among the things that support this is «the Prophet's ﷺ permission for Asma' bint Abi Bakr al-Siddiq to maintain ties with her mother while she was a disbeliever». Some scholars said that her story is the cause of the revelation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over the religion﴾, and the verse [al-Mumtahina: 8].

**The Qur'anic verse:** ﴿And do not turn your cheek away from people﴾.

Its meaning: do not be arrogant toward people. The verse forbids arrogance toward people. *Al-ṣa'r* (ṣuʿr) means inclining, and *al-ṣa'r* (the term) originally refers to a disease that afflicts the camel, causing it to twist its neck. It is applied to the arrogant person who twists his neck and turns his cheek away from people out of pride toward them. From this is the verse of ʿAmr ibn Ḥunayy al-Taghlibi:

؎We were, when a tyrant turned his cheek aside, we straightened him from his inclination, and he stood upright.

And the verse of Abu Ṭalib:

؎We were of old not accepting injustice, *** when they twisted their haughty heads, we would straighten them.

(p-181) From the application of *al-ṣa'r* to inclination is the verse of al-Namir ibn Tawlab al-ʿAllaki:

؎Indeed we came to you when the journey had grown long, *** leading lean horses, among them those with bent necks.

Since you know that the meaning of His words ﴿And do not turn your cheek away from people﴾ is: do not be arrogant toward them.

Know that we have already presented, in the discussion of His words ﴿So it is not for you to be arrogant therein, so get out; indeed you are of the debased﴾ [al-A'raf: 13], in Surat "al-A'raf," the Qur'anic verses that indicate warning against pride and clarify the abundance of its evil consequences. We also explained that, along with some verses indicating the goodness of humility and Allah's praise of the humble.

His words ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly﴾.

We have already presented its explanation and the interpretation of the verse in Surat "Banu Isra'il," in the discussion of His words ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly; indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart] or reach the mountains in height﴾ [al-Isra': 37].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 19:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And be moderate in your walk﴾.

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in several places, such as His saying: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ [al-Furqan: 63], and His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly﴾ [al-Isra': 37].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among people is one who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book﴾ (20). We have already explained this in the beginning of Surat "al-Hajj".

And likewise His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Even if Satan were calling them to the punishment of the blazing Fire?﴾ (21). We have already presented the verses that clarify this point, also at the beginning of Surah "al-Hajj," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is decreed for him that whoever takes him as an ally, he will mislead him and guide him to the punishment of the blazing Fire﴾ [al-Hajj: 4].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 25:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, "Allah." Say, "All praise is for Allah." But most of them do not know.﴾ (25)

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Bani Isra'il," in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable﴾ [Al-Isra': 9].

(p-182) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens and the sea, replenished by seven more seas after it, were ink, the words of Allah would not be exhausted.﴾

We have already explained this in Surah "al-Kahf," in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would surely be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as replenishment﴾ [al-Kahf: 109].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 28:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are but as a single soul.﴾

We have already clarified this at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah, in the discussion of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Thus does Allah bring the dead to life and shows you His signs﴾ [al-Baqarah: 73], and so on.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 32:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion.﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this in Surah "Bani Isra'il" (Surat al-Isra'), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him﴾ [al-Isra' 17:67], and in "al-An'am" (Surat al-An'am), in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you or the Hour comes upon you, would you call upon other than Allah, if you should be truthful?" Rather, it is Him you call upon﴾ [al-An'am 6:40-41], and elsewhere.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 33:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord and dread a Day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all﴾, to the end of the verse.

This verse, by its apparent meaning, indicates that on the Day of Resurrection a parent will not benefit his child. Yet another verse has come indicating the elevation of the ranks of children because of the righteousness of their parents, so that they may be in the rank of their parents, even though their own deeds did not reach that rank, as a comfort to the eyes of the parents by the presence of their children with them in their abodes in Paradise, and that is a benefit for them. It is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith, We will join with them their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything from their deeds﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Tur: 21].

The way of reconciling them is indicated by the restriction found in this verse, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and whose descendants followed them in faith﴾. The benefit is specified in it, in that their joining with them in their ranks is conditioned by faith. Thus it is more specific than the other verse, and the more specific does not contradict the more general. And according to the view of one who interpreted the verse as meaning that His saying, ﴿no father will avail his son﴾, means that he will not discharge for him a right that was incumbent upon him, nor will he repel from him a punishment that was decreed against him, then there is no difficulty in the verse.

More elaboration on this will come in surah "al-Najm," in the discussion of: ﴿And that man will have nothing except what he strives for﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Najm: 39], God willing.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 31, verse 34:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs. And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.﴾ (34).

We have already mentioned in surah al-An'am that these five mentioned at the end of surah Luqman are the keys of the unseen (mafatih al-ghayb) mentioned in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him﴾ [al-An'am: 59], and that the Prophet (ﷺ) clarified that by means of the authentic Sunnah.
